Attention Variants · The KV Cache05

LLM Inference with a KV Cache

We can make LLM inference more efficient by using a KV Cache

KV Cache: a "dictionary" that stores all of our previously computed Ks and Vs so we can re-use them (instead of needing to recalculate them) with future tokens

In multi-head attention, each head has its own KV Cache

Attention Variants · Variants13

LLM Inference: Prefill and Decode

LLM inference can be broken down into two separate steps: Prefill and Decode

Prefill: reading phase where the model processes your entire input prompt all at once in parallel (this fills the KV cache).

Decode: writing phase where the model generates the output response one token at a time, sequentially.

Variant 5: DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA)

DeepSeek V3.2 (DSA + MLA) and GLM-5

We calculate an importance score for each token and attend to only the k most important ones (this would be top_k=4):

I_{t,s} = \sum_j ω_{t,j}\,\mathrm{ReLU}\bp{q_{t,j}\cdot k_s}
Attention Variants · Variants18

Variant 6: Gated Attention

Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, Arcee Trinity Large 400B (typically combined with Hybrid Attention)

Essentially we just add an extra weight matrix (a gate) before adding the residual. The original Gated Attention paper found it adds some non-linearity and gets rid of the "attention sink", and Qwen3-Next uses it for the full-attention layers it keeps inside a hybrid stack.

Attention Variants · Variants19

Variant 7: Hybrid Attention (Gated DeltaNet)

Qwen3-Next (very tricky)

Like an RNN

  • Fixed-size state carried token to token
  • Constant memory and work per token at decode: no growing KV cache
  • Gates decide what to forget (α) and what to write (β), like LSTM / GRU
  • Qwen3-Next: 3 of every 4 layers are Gated DeltaNet

Not like an RNN

  • State is a matrix of key → value pairs (64 × 64 per head here), not a vector
  • Update is linear in S (no tanh): chunk-parallel training, no BPTT
  • Read-out qₜ Sₜ is linear attention (no softmax): weaker exact recall, so 1 Gated Attention layer per 3

Attention Variants · Variants22

Flash Attention (very important)

  • Same answer, computed smarter: Flash Attention doesn't change what attention does
  • A GPU has two kinds of memory: a small, very fast workbench and a huge, slow warehouse
  • Standard attention keeps making trips to the warehouse: it stores the giant N × N score table, then fetches it back
  • The GPU spends most of its time waiting on those trips, not doing math
  • Flash works on small tiles at the workbench and only writes down the final result
  • Payoff: far less memory and several × faster, so much longer inputs fit
  • The trick: softmax can be updated tile by tile using running totals
  • Works alongside the variants in this lecture: they change what is computed, Flash changes how

Technically, the workbench is SRAM and the warehouse is HBM
